Priya K.: Hi all, I accepted the org invite but hitting 403 when trying to push to github.com/redwood-inference/serving. The repo shows "Request access". I already have 2FA enabled. Any pointers? :slightly_frowning_face:

Alex (DevEx): Welcome! First check: are you signed into the same GitHub account locally that accepted the invite? Common gotcha is using a personal account for git while the invite was to the work account.

Priya K.: I think I accepted with priya@redwood.email but my laptop git ssh config has my old key tied to priya-personal. How can I confirm which account GitHub sees for SSH pushes?

Samira (IT): For SSH, GitHub matches the SSH key to the account that uploaded it. Try:
```bash
ssh -T git@github.com
```
You should see a message like: "Hi username! You've successfully authenticated..." that shows which GH account the key belongs to.

Priya K.: Running that returns: "Hi priya-personal! You've successfully authenticated." OK that explains it. What's the recommended path? Replace the SSH key, or add the personal account to the org?

Alex (DevEx): We generally prefer using the work account for company repos. Two options: (A) add your work SSH key to the work GitHub account and use that, or (B) if you prefer using the personal account, we can add that account to the org and map it to the proper team. Note company policy wants commits to be linked to your company identity for compliance.

onboarding-bot: Note: invite sent to priya@redwood.email (10:15am).

Priya K.: I'll switch my laptop to the work account key. Do I need to remove the personal key entirely?

Samira (IT): You can keep both keys but ensure ssh config selects the correct key for github.com. For example, add to ~/.ssh/config:
```
Host github.com
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa_priya_work
```
Then test again with ssh -T.

Alex (DevEx): After you confirm the SSH key maps to the work account and you've authorized SSO (if prompted), the repo should become accessible. If it still shows "Request access", ping me and I'll trigger a team sync.

Priya K.: Done the ssh config change and added the key to priya@redwood.email. ssh -T now shows "Hi priya-redwood!". I also authorized SSO when prompted. I can clone and push now. Thanks for the clear steps! :tada:
